title: Does This Action Still Explain the Task? Reverse Scoring for Diffusion Language Model Agents
abstract: arXiv:2609.38536v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Diffusion-based large language models (dLLMs) promise to break the sequential latency bottleneck of autoregressive agents through parallel decoding, but recent evaluations show this efficiency does not transfer to embodied agentic competence: dLLM-backed agents repeatedly fall into retry loops, re-issuing an action long after it has failed. We give a mechanistic account of this failure and a training-free remedy. We trace the retry loop to the adaptivity of masked decoding: the sampler commits the positions it is most confident about and defers the uncertain ones, and at a failure state the context already offers a confident fill for the deferred decision, i.e. the failed action itself, so the retry is committed without the failure feedback ever being confronted. translated_title: 这个动作还能解释任务吗？面向扩散语言模型智能体的反向评分
translated_abstract: 基于扩散的大语言模型承诺通过并行解码打破自回归智能体的顺序延迟瓶颈，但近期评估表明，这种效率优势并未转化为具身智能体能力：由 dLLM 驱动的智能体反复陷入重试循环，在动作早已失败之后仍不断重复发出同一动作。我们对这一失败给出了机理层面的解释，并提供了一种无需训练的补救方案。我们将重试循环归因于掩码解码的自适应性：采样器会先提交其最有把握的位置，而推迟不确定的位置；在失败状态下，上下文已经为被推迟的决策提供了一个“有把握”的填充——即那个刚刚失败的动作本身——于是重试在未真正面对失败反馈的情况下就被提交了。我们将由此导致的动作分布扭曲建模为一种任务盲的破坏：上下文中显著的动作（例如刚刚执行过的动作）会获得被夸大的概率……
tldr: 该文揭示了扩散语言模型智能体反复重试已失败动作的机理根源——掩码解码的自适应性使上下文中刚失败的“显著动作”获得被夸大的概率——并提出一种无需训练的“反向评分”方法来纠正这种任务盲的分布扭曲。
en_tdlr: The paper mechanistically traces dLLM agents' retry loops to adaptive masked decoding, which inflates the probability of contextually salient just-failed actions, and proposes a training-free "reverse scoring" remedy for this task-blind distributional corruption.
